sentences.en: So there's a serious point here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有个严肃的观点。

sentences.en: Sir Lee Teebing in this book basically says everything in Christmas, in Christianity, is invented.

sentences.en: And all the elements of the nativity story have basically been plagiarized from rival cults in the days of the Roman Empire, I suppose.

sentences.en: And actually, Tom, the serious point is, you see this idea repeated all the time.
sentences.zh: 其实，汤姆，严肃的观点在于，你会发现这种观点一直被反复提及。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very popular.
sentences.zh: 是的，它非常流行。

sentences.en: So keen humanists and atheists are always saying, well, actually, I think you'll find that if Jesus existed, which he didn't, he definitely wasn't born on December the 25th.
sentences.zh: 所以热心的人文主义者和无神论者总是说，好吧，其实如果你去查证一下，如果耶稣真的存在——虽然他并不存在——他绝对不是出生在12月25日。

sentences.en: And everything is ripped off from Mithraism or from Sol Invictus or all of these other religions.
sentences.zh: 而且一切都是从密特拉教、无敌太阳神或其他宗教那里抄袭来的。

sentences.en: Well, we did two episodes on Jesus, didn't we, last time as our festive offering.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们上次作为节日献礼，专门做了两期关于耶稣的节目，不是吗？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们做了。

sentences.en: And I think we agreed that Jesus probably wasn't born on 25th of December.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都同意耶稣可能不是出生在12月25日。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know when he's born and we don't know which year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们不知道他什么时候出生，也不知道是哪一年。

sentences.en: But this is not quite what Sir Lee Teebing is saying.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是李·提宾爵士所说的全部。

sentences.en: He's essentially saying that Christmas is ultimately a pagan festival and that Christians have stolen various aspects of pagan cults and kind of bundled it all together to create a kind of pagan mismatch that they're passing off as their own festival.

sentences.en: And this is quite a popular theory, as you say.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这是一种相当流行的理论。

sentences.en: So popular that until you put me right about two years ago, I believed it to be true myself.
sentences.zh: 流行到在大约两年前你纠正我之前，连我自己都相信这是真的。

sentences.en: Did you?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I believed that it had been ripped off from other Roman rivals.
sentences.zh: 我曾经相信它是从其他罗马竞争对手那里抄来的。

sentences.en: Well, so the question of whether it's a pagan festival, I mean, that's what we're going to be looking at today.
sentences.zh: 好吧，关于它是否是一个异教节日的问题，这就是我们今天要探讨的内容。

sentences.en: But one thing I think we can absolutely say is that it is a Roman festival.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们可以绝对肯定的一点是，它是一个罗马节日。

sentences.en: It originates as a Roman festival because obviously Jesus was born into the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 它起源于一个罗马节日，因为显然耶稣出生在罗马帝国。

sentences.en: And the center of early Christian activity was within the limits of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 而早期基督教活动的中心就在罗马帝国的范围内。

sentences.en: I mean, not exclusively, but mostly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不完全是，但主要是这样。

sentences.en: So I think you could say that Christmas is one of the festivals that grows up over the course of Roman history.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你可以说圣诞节是随着罗马历史进程而成长起来的节日之一。

sentences.en: But does this make it a pagan festival?
sentences.zh: 但这能让它成为一个异教节日吗？

sentences.en: So that's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: The tantalizing question.
sentences.zh: 一个诱人的问题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, there are kind of various elements to what Salih was claiming.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，萨利所声称的内容有各种各样的要素。

sentences.en: We should remind ourselves, Salih TV obviously doesn't exiSt.

sentences.en: That's poor.
sentences.zh: 那很糟糕。

sentences.zh: 但他确实这么说了。

sentences.en: So although in the book, he's actually British.
sentences.zh: 虽然在书中，他实际上是英国人。

sentences.en: So that's another thing to chalk up to Dan Brown's mastery.
sentences.zh: 所以这是丹·布朗“大师级”水平的又一个例证。

sentences.en: Dan Brown's solecism.
sentences.zh: 丹·布朗的失言。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 所以他说前基督教神祇密特拉出生于12月25日。

sentences.zh: 印度神祇克里希纳，获赠了黄金、乳香和没药。

sentences.en: So, you know, these are gods from quite a broad range of backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这些神祇来自非常广泛的背景。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果所有这些神都出生在同一天的话。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I have a lot of confidence, both in Lee Teabing and indeed in Dan Brown.
sentences.zh: 我对李·提宾和丹·布朗都非常有信心。

sentences.en: I mean, we established earlier this year that Dan Brown is very rarely wrong about religious history, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们今年早些时候确定过，丹·布朗在宗教历史方面很少出错，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, have his senses misled him on this occasion?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那这次他的感官是否误导了他？

sentences.en: There is not a single ancient source that states that Osiris or Adonis or Dionysus were born on the 25th of December.
sentences.zh: 没有任何古代文献记载奥西里斯、阿多尼斯或狄俄尼索斯出生于12月25日。

sentences.en: Absolutely none.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: And in fact, Osiris, so he's a very, very significant Egyptian god.
sentences.zh: 事实上，奥西里斯，他是一位非常非常重要的埃及神祇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we talked about him in our episode on the death of Antinous, Hadrian's beloved, who drowns in the Nile.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于哈德良的爱人安提诺乌斯之死的节目中谈到过他，他淹死在尼罗河里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Osiris becomes the god of the dead.
sentences.zh: 奥西里斯成为了死神。

sentences.en: And so the date of his death and the date of his birth are both seen as being very significant, rather as in the Christian story.
sentences.zh: 所以他的死亡日期和出生日期都被认为非常重要，就像基督教故事中那样。

sentences.en: But Osiris is not born on the same day as Jesus.
sentences.zh: 但奥西里斯并不是和耶稣同一天出生的。

sentences.zh: 但基本上，他似乎出生在九月初。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: No evidence for this at all.
sentences.zh: 根本没有证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: So all of this is, I don't know where he's, well, I do know where he's got it from.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切，我不知道他是从哪儿……好吧，我知道他是从哪儿弄来的。

sentences.en: He's basically, he's extrapolating from kind of 19th century scholars who are putting a particular spin on it, and he is hyping it up a bit.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是从19世纪的学者那里推断出来的，那些学者对它进行了特定的解读，而他把这些炒作了一番。

sentences.en: I mean, that's essentially where it's kind of come from.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上就是它的来源。

sentences.en: But there are no ancient sources for any of this.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些都没有古代文献支持。

sentences.en: But he does mention this god, Mithras, the pre-Christian god, Mithras.
sentences.zh: 但他确实提到了这个神，密特拉，前基督教神祇密特拉。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love Mithras.

sentences.en: I can't remember.

sentences.en: They'd have their little clubs and they'd meet underground and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的小俱乐部，在地下聚会之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So is he a pre-Christian god, Mithras, as Silly Teabing claims?
sentences.zh: 那么，像萨利·提宾声称的那样，密特拉是前基督教神祇吗？

sentences.en: Slightly steadier ground here, because there is a Persian god called, not Mithras, but Mithra.
sentences.zh: 这里的基础稍微稳固一点，因为有一位波斯神祇叫密特拉（Mithra），而不是密特拉（Mithras）。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Who is, he's kind of pre-Zorastrian, probably.

sentences.en: So very, very ancient.
sentences.zh: 所以非常非常古老。

sentences.en: And Mithras is clearly a variant form of that name, Mithra.
sentences.zh: 而密特拉（Mithras）显然是那个名字密特拉（Mithra）的变体形式。

sentences.en: And there is a reference to a god called Mithras being worshipped before the birth of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有关于一位叫密特拉的神在基督诞生前就受到崇拜的记载。

sentences.en: And it comes in Plutarch in his biography of Pompey the Great, Caesar's great rival.
sentences.zh: 它出现在普鲁塔克的《大庞培传》中，那是凯撒的劲敌。

sentences.en: One of his great feats was to defeat the pirates who were kind of naval terrorists roaming the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他的一大功绩是击败了那些在在地中海游荡的海上恐怖分子——海盗。

sentences.en: And Plutarch says that the pirates who were defeated by Pompey practiced the secret mysteries of Mithras.
sentences.zh: 普鲁塔克说，被庞培击败的海盗们信奉密特拉的秘密仪式。

sentences.en: But the consensus would be that this probably isn't the same as the cult of Mithras that gets practiced by Roman officers, kind of Roman equivalent of Freemasons.
sentences.zh: 但共识是，这可能与罗马军官们信奉的密特拉教派——即罗马版的共济会——不是同一个东西。

sentences.en: Because the origins of this seem to be the first century AD.
sentences.zh: 因为这个教派的起源似乎是在公元一世纪。

sentences.en: And it seems to have originated in Rome, so not in the EaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且它似乎起源于罗马，而不是东方。

sentences.en: And a bit, again, a bit like Freemasonry, that it's a kind of brotherhood that is drawing on all kinds of different traditions to garnish it,
sentences.zh: 而且，再次像共济会一样，它是一种兄弟会，利用各种不同的传统来装饰自己，

sentences.en: to make it look a little bit more kind of exotic.
sentences.zh: 让它看起来更有异国情调。

sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上从另一个宗教那里借用了密特拉这个名字，或者说密特拉（Mithra），来让自己看起来更迷人、更具异国情调和刺激感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 所以这是一种东方主义、异国情调的门面装饰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 所以我认为萨利在那点上是错的。

sentences.zh: 他说密特拉被埋在岩石里也是错的。

sentences.en: He wasn't.
sentences.zh: 他并没有。

sentences.en: Instead, Mithras emerges fully formed from a rock, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 相反，密特拉似乎是从岩石中完整地诞生出来的。

sentences.en: And there don't seem to be any references at all, certainly, that I've been able to find in ancient sources, to his dying and being reborn on the third day.

sentences.zh: 你可以命令一个人大声说出关于他自己的某个丢脸的秘密，命令另一个人跳裸舞，抱起吹笛女，绕着房间跑三圈。

sentences.zh: 而且显然，你知道，你被称为“第一公民”。

sentences.zh: 有一个著名的例子，一位未来的皇帝确实被投票选为“第一公民”。

sentences.zh: 这就是尼禄。

sentences.en: And according to Tacitus, Nero gets voted princeps of their kind of group of friends.
sentences.zh: 据塔西佗记载，尼禄被他们那群朋友投票选为“第一公民”。

sentences.en: And he gets his stepbrother, Britannicus, who is the son of Claudius, to stand in the middle of the party and sing a song.
sentences.zh: 他让他的继兄弟不列塔尼库斯——也就是克劳狄的儿子——站在聚会中间唱歌。

sentences.en: And Britannicus sings a sad song about how Claudius' dad is shoving him to one side and allowing Nero perhaps to become emperor.
sentences.zh: 不列塔尼库斯唱了一首悲伤的歌，讲述克劳狄的父亲如何将他排挤到一边，却让尼禄有机会成为皇帝。

sentences.en: So it could be a moment for pathos as well as fun.
sentences.zh: 所以这既是一个充满悲情，又是一个充满乐趣的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the one thing about it that is kind of reminiscent of Christmas, and I think it's the thing that people always pick up on, is that people gave each other presents.
sentences.zh: 关于它有一点很像圣诞节，而且我认为这是人们总是会注意到的地方，那就是人们互相赠送礼物。

sentences.en: So they give each other candles and they give each other dolls that are called Sigilaria.
sentences.zh: 他们互赠蜡烛，还赠送一种叫“西吉拉里亚”的人偶。

sentences.en: And some of these are images of gods.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是神的形象。

sentences.zh: 大多数都非常便宜。

sentences.en: They're kind of mass produced, but they can be very rich, kind of very expensively done.
sentences.zh: 它们算是批量生产的，但也可以做得非常精致、昂贵。

sentences.en: And Macrobius, who is a guy writing in the Christian period, the late fourth century, and he's very, very nostalgic for the festivities of the Saturnalia.
sentences.zh: 马克罗比乌斯，一位生活在基督教时期、即公元四世纪末的作家，他对农神节的庆祝活动怀有非常强烈的怀旧之情。

sentences.en: And he and his friends have a big debate about, you know, what are these dolls?
sentences.zh: 他和朋友们进行了一场大辩论，讨论这些玩偶到底是什么？

sentences.en: Are they substitutes for the sacrifices that were originally made to Saturn?
sentences.zh: 它们是最初献给农神的祭品的替代品吗？

sentences.en: Or are they just toys?
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅是玩具？

sentences.en: And they can't decide, which is quite a kind of modern sounding debate.
sentences.zh: 他们无法做出定论，这听起来是一场相当现代的辩论。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like the kind of debates that, you know, scholars would have today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来像是今天学者们会进行的辩论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 它们是用粘土、石膏之类的材料做的。

sentences.en: France Dupont, who writes, she's written a brilliant book on everyday life in the Roman Republic, daily life in ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 弗朗斯·杜邦写过一本关于罗马共和国日常生活、古罗马日常生活的精彩著作。

sentences.en: She writes about the Saturnalia.
sentences.zh: 她写到了农神节。

sentences.en: For one day, nothing was as it seemed, neither the relationships between people nor the presence that changed hands.
sentences.zh: 在那一天，一切都显得虚假，无论是人与人之间的关系，还是易手的礼物。

sentences.en: Order would return on the following day.
sentences.zh: 秩序会在第二天恢复。

sentences.en: Anarchy, chance, deceptive appearance.
sentences.zh: 无政府状态、偶然性、虚假的表象。

sentences.zh: 农神节是罗马公民真实生活的反面。

sentences.en: And so it seems to be a kind of safety valve to slaves to cast off the kind of the traditional order.

sentences.en: On the thing with the slaves, I mean, presumably there were bounds that they couldn't overstep.
sentences.zh: 关于奴隶那件事，我想，大概还是有一些他们不能逾越的界限吧。

sentences.en: So, you know, they can talk back to their masters.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们可以顶撞主人。

sentences.en: But I mean, the next day they're going to be slaves again and their masters will remember.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，第二天他们又会变回奴隶，而主人会记得这一切。

sentences.en: So, of course, it's probably not quite as this wonderful release.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，这可能并不完全是一种美妙的释放。

sentences.en: Because it must be, to some degree, if you've got a very horrible master, the whole thing must just be this grotesque parody that you have to go through.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你有一个非常糟糕的主人，在某种程度上，这一切一定只是一场你不得不经历的怪诞闹剧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 总之，抱歉，你继续。

sentences.zh: 不，不，我的意思是，你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: That, of course, every slave knows that once the Saturnalia is gone, you know, the master can absolutely punish you for anything that you said.
sentences.zh: 当然，每个奴隶都知道，一旦农神节结束，主人完全可以因为你说的任何话而惩罚你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I think the idea is that it gives, you know, a slave, it gives a slave the chance to make a complaint that he or she might think that the owner would be amenable to.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这个想法是，它给了奴隶一个机会，去提出他或她认为主人可能会接受的抱怨。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's kind of a little bit like that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得有点像那样。

sentences.en: But you're right that, of course, you know, there are lots of people who don't like it, chiefly intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对，当然，有很多不喜欢它的人，主要是知识分子。

sentences.zh: 一些知识分子似乎真的很讨厌农神节。

sentences.zh: 所以我们之前提到的塞内卡，抱怨农神节全年都在进行。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He hates having to discard his toga because he feels that it infringes his dignity.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌不得不脱掉托加长袍，因为他觉得这有损他的尊严。

sentences.en: And he says that it's disrespectful to the ancestors of the Roman people who had only ever discarded their togas when the Republic was in peril and fallen on evil days.
sentences.zh: 他说这对罗马人民的祖先是不敬的，因为祖先们只有在共和国处于危险和陷入困境时才会脱掉托加长袍。

sentences.en: And Pliny the Younger, who's an absolute funster, when everybody is having fun and celebrating Saturnalia, he retreats to his study and reads.
sentences.zh: 而小普林尼，那个绝对的“扫兴者”，当每个人都在享受农神节的快乐时，他却躲进书房读书。

sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，你可以读读看。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 嗯，读书是圣诞节做的一件好事。

sentences.en: And you think, well, I'm going to go home.
sentences.zh: 你会想，好吧，我要回家了。

sentences.zh: 我要读点狄更斯。

sentences.zh: 在书房里读点狄更斯。

sentences.en: But it has to be said that Roman poets seem to have adored it.
sentences.zh: 但必须说，罗马诗人似乎非常喜爱它。

sentences.en: So Catullus, great love poet, contemporary of Julius Caesar.
sentences.zh: 比如卡图卢斯，伟大的爱情诗人，尤利乌斯·凯撒的同时代人。

sentences.en: He called it the best of days.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“最好的日子”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Statius, poet writing under Domitian.
sentences.zh: 斯塔提乌斯，在图密善统治下写作的诗人。

sentences.en: He celebrated a lavish Saturnalia that had been hosted by the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他庆祝了由皇帝主持的奢华的农神节。

sentences.en: And Horace intriguingly gives us a flavor of what it might have been like outside Rome.
sentences.zh: 而贺拉斯有趣地为我们提供了一点罗马城外可能是什么样子的风味。

sentences.en: Because in one of his poems, he describes how every December there's this local cult, this village feast, which is in honor not of Saturn, but of Faunus,
sentences.zh: 因为在他的一首诗中，他描述了每年十二月都有一个当地的崇拜活动，一个乡村盛宴，不是为了纪念农神，而是为了纪念法乌努斯，

sentences.en: the king with the goat horns.
sentences.zh: 那个长着山羊角的国王。

sentences.en: And it sounds quite like the Saturnalia.
sentences.zh: 听起来很像农神节。

sentences.en: So he sacrifices lots of produce.
sentences.zh: 所以他献祭了大量的农产品。

sentences.en: He throws big parties.
sentences.zh: 他举办大型派对。

sentences.en: Lots of presents go out.
sentences.zh: 分发大量的礼物。

sentences.en: It's a season of plenty.
sentences.zh: 这是一个丰收的季节。

sentences.en: And then they all go out into the fields.
sentences.zh: 然后他们都走到田野里。

sentences.en: And they all have a big dance, big knees up, surrounded by their cattle.
sentences.zh: 他们在牛群的环绕下跳舞、狂欢。

sentences.en: And it all sounds great fun.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常有趣。

sentences.en: So I think philosophers, intellectuals, they don't like Saturnalia.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为哲学家、知识分子不喜欢农神节。

sentences.en: Poets, they absolutely seem to have loved it.
sentences.zh: 而诗人们似乎绝对热爱它。

sentences.en: And I think it's clear from this that December was associated with merrymaking and that the Saturnalia, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为由此可以清楚地看出，十二月与狂欢有关，而且农神节，你知道，

sentences.en: because it clearly has influenced the celebration of Faunus out in the fields.
sentences.zh: 因为它显然影响了田野里对法乌努斯的庆祝活动。

sentences.zh: 那么问题是，它是否影响了其他崇拜？

sentences.zh: 我们已经指出了这一点。

sentences.zh: 这两个节日实际上在整个古典时代晚期是同时庆祝的。

sentences.zh: 所以你可以过农神节，然后过圣诞节。

sentences.zh: 所以它们并不是很明显地融合在一起。

sentences.zh: 你知道，直到四世纪甚至五世纪，它们仍被视为独立的节日。

sentences.en: Would people do both if you're a bit promiscuous about your religion?
sentences.zh: 如果你对宗教比较“博爱”，你会两者都过吗？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有基督徒非常讨厌这一点。

sentences.zh: 但是的，我认为确实有人两者都过。

sentences.en: Ah.

sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.zh: 这种选举一位可以组织娱乐活动的“第一公民”的想法。

sentences.zh: 这看起来很像圣诞节庆祝活动中的“混乱之王”。

sentences.en: And the idea that the Lord of Misrule, the medieval Lord of Misrule, is descended from the kind of Saturnalian figure is very, very popular in the late Victorian period.
sentences.zh: 而且“混乱之王”——中世纪的“混乱之王”——源自农神节人物的观点在维多利亚时代晚期非常流行。

sentences.en: So James Fraser, who wrote The Golden Bower, he's all over that.
sentences.zh: 所以写了《金枝》的詹姆斯·弗雷泽对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: But the Lord of Misrule is a medieval tradition.
sentences.zh: 但“混乱之王”是中世纪的传统。

sentences.en: There doesn't seem to be anything that joins it to antiquity.
sentences.zh: 似乎没有任何东西能把它与古代联系起来。

sentences.en: So basically it seems convergent evolution.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这似乎是趋同进化。

sentences.en: So the way that just because a bird, a pterosaur, and a bat all have wings doesn't mean that they have all evolved from one another.
sentences.zh: 就像鸟类、翼龙和蝙蝠都有翅膀，并不意味着它们是彼此进化而来的。

sentences.en: And of course the whole idea that Christmas festivities originated in Saturnalian celebrations, it doesn't originate with atheists or humanists.
sentences.zh: 当然，圣诞节庆祝活动起源于农神节庆祝活动的整个想法，并不是起源于无神论者或人文主义者。

sentences.zh: 它起源于想要废除所有这种狂欢的清教徒。

sentences.zh: 所以克伦威尔派，没错。

sentences.en: And so they recognize, I think, that these celebrations, you know, they're an inheritance from the Catholic past, from before the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们认识到，这些庆祝活动是天主教过去的遗产，是宗教改革之前的遗产。

sentences.zh: 把它们定性为异教，使他们更容易废除它们。

sentences.zh: 它们都在十二月。

sentences.zh: 但这随之引发了一个问题，基督徒是否因为这个原因特意选择了12月25日？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为他们选择这一天是因为它是“无敌太阳”的生日。

sentences.en: I don't think they choose it because of Saturnalia, for the reasons that I've explained.
sentences.zh: 基于我解释的原因，我不认为他们是因为农神节而选择这一天。

sentences.en: And actually, we know, I think, why the Christians choose December the 25th, despite the fact that there is no evidence whatsoever in the Gospels for him being born on that day.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为我们知道基督徒为什么选择12月25日，尽管福音书中没有任何证据表明他出生在那一天。

sentences.en: And they do it quite late.
sentences.zh: 而且他们选择的时间相当晚。

sentences.en: So the reason that it takes Christians so long, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以基督徒花这么长时间的原因，你知道，

sentences.en: we said that the earliest mention of Christmas being celebrated on the 25th of December isn't until the middle of the 4th century.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，最早提到12月25日庆祝圣诞节的记录要到四世纪中叶才出现。

sentences.en: And the reason for that, I think, is that Christians viewed the celebration of birthdays as a pagan practice.
sentences.zh: 我认为其原因是，基督徒将庆祝生日视为一种异教习俗。

sentences.en: So Oregon, the great philosopher, possibly a eunuch, he writes a commentary on the Gospel of St. Matthew.
sentences.zh: 所以伟大的哲学家奥利金，可能是一位太监，他写了一篇关于《圣马太福音》的注释。

sentences.en: And in it, he observes that we learn from Scripture that no birthday was ever celebrated by a righteous man.
sentences.zh: 在文中，他观察到我们从经文中得知，义人从不庆祝生日。

sentences.en: Oh, why?
sentences.zh: 哦，为什么？

sentences.en: Why wouldn't you celebrate someone's birthday?
sentences.zh: 为什么不庆祝某人的生日呢？

sentences.en: Mad.
sentences.zh: 疯了。

sentences.en: It's seen as a pagan, a thing that pagans do.
sentences.zh: 这被视为异教徒的行为，是异教徒做的事。

sentences.en: It's not something that Jews or, and therefore by extension, Christians are doing.
sentences.zh: 这不是犹太人，或者推而广之，基督徒会做的事。

sentences.en: So then why did they start doing it in the mid-4th century?
sentences.zh: 那么他们为什么在公元四世纪中叶开始这样做呢？

sentences.en: And I think it's all to do with debates about who or what Christ was.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全与关于基督是谁或什么的争论有关。

sentences.en: You know, to what extent is he divine?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在多大程度上是神？

sentences.en: To what extent is he human?
sentences.zh: 他在多大程度上是人？

sentences.en: And there are lots of people, lots of Christians who are saying that Christ is purely divine, and therefore the man Jesus is born, and then the divine Christ enters him.
sentences.zh: 有很多人，很多基督徒说基督纯粹是神，因此耶稣作为人出生，然后神性的基督进入了他体内。

sentences.en: This is not what comes to be orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 这并不是后来成为正统观念的内容。

sentences.en: So at the Council of Nicaea in 325, they declare that Jesus is God of God, light of light, very God of very God, but also that he came down and was incarnate,
sentences.zh: 所以在公元325年的尼西亚公会议上，他们宣布耶稣是神之神，光之光，真神之真神，但也宣布他降临并道成肉身，

sentences.en: i.e. made flesh and was made man.
sentences.zh: 即化作血肉，成为人。

sentences.en: So therefore, if you're trying to see off people who think that Jesus wasn't really man, it's important to identify his birthday.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想驳斥那些认为耶稣并非真正的人的人，确定他的生日就很重要。

sentences.en: And that's why I think it's shortly after the Council of Nicaea that you start getting celebration of his birthday.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为在尼西亚公会议后不久，你就开始看到对耶稣生日的庆祝了。

sentences.en: But that, of course, still doesn't explain why it's the 25th of December.
sentences.zh: 但这当然还是不能解释为什么是12月25日。

sentences.en: And I think that, as you would expect, the reason for it lies in Christian reasons, just as the Saturnalia is held for reasons that have to do with the worship of Saturn.
sentences.zh: 我认为，正如你所料，其原因在于基督教内部，就像农神节的举行是为了崇拜农神一样。

sentences.en: So Christmas is celebrated on the deities for reasons that have to do with the inheritance of Jewish tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以圣诞节在这些神祇的日子里庆祝，是因为继承了犹太传统。

sentences.en: And both Jewish and Christian scholars are very, very into the idea that the great calendar of the ages has an inherent symmetry.
sentences.zh: 犹太学者和基督教学者都非常非常沉迷于这样一个观点：伟大的时代历法具有内在的对称性。

sentences.en: So Jewish scholars, they argue that the creation of the world, the birth of Abraham, Abraham's heirs,
sentences.zh: 犹太学者认为，世界的创造、亚伯拉罕的诞生、亚伯拉罕的后裔，

sentences.en: that they are all born on the same day that will be the day when the Messiah is born and Israel gains its redemption.
sentences.zh: 他们都出生在同一天，而这一天也将是弥赛亚诞生和以色列获得救赎的日子。

sentences.en: So this idea that there's a kind of a patterning that's stamped by God on the flow of time.
sentences.zh: 所以这种观点认为，上帝在时间流逝中印下了一种模式。

sentences.en: And Christian scholars inherit this.
sentences.zh: 而基督教学者继承了这一点。

sentences.en: And for the same reason, they come to believe that Jesus had died on the anniversary of his incarnation.
sentences.zh: 出于同样的原因，他们开始相信耶稣死于他道成肉身的那一天。

sentences.en: So in other words, Christ comes into the world on the same day that he leaves it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，基督来到世上的日子，正是他离开世上的日子。

sentences.en: And there is therefore a kind of a perfect symmetry to the structure of his life and death.
sentences.zh: 因此，他生与死的结构有一种完美的对称性。

sentences.en: When you say he came into the world, is that being born or being conceived?
sentences.zh: 当你提到他来到世上时，是指出生还是受孕？

sentences.en: No, it's the incarnation.
sentences.zh: 不，是指道成肉身。

sentences.en: So it's when the Archangel Gabriel appears to the Virgin Mary and Jesus becomes incarnate.
sentences.zh: 也就是天使加百列向圣母玛利亚显现，耶稣道成肉身的时候。

sentences.en: He is conceived in her womb.
sentences.zh: 他在她的子宫里受孕。

sentences.en: And this date for complicated reasons that I won't go into, but it's to do with the dating of the Passover and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 这个日期出于复杂的原因，我就不细说了，但它与逾越节的日期以及各种事情有关。

sentences.en: Christians, first in Carthage and then in Rome, come to identify this with the 25th of March.
sentences.zh: 基督徒们，先是在迦太基，后来在罗马，开始将这一天定为3月25日。

sentences.en: So this is Lady Day.
sentences.zh: 这就是圣母领报节。

sentences.en: It's the day that Tolkien identifies as being the day on which the ring is thrown into the crack of doom.
sentences.zh: 托尔金认为这一天就是魔戒被扔进末日裂缝的日子。

sentences.en: To Mount Doom.
sentences.zh: 扔进末日火山。

sentences.en: It's the holiest day of the year.
sentences.zh: 这是全年最神圣的日子。

sentences.en: I mean, Tolkien, of course, absolutely knew this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，托尔金当然完全知道这一点。

sentences.en: And this beds down, I think, over the second, the third, into the fourth century.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在二世纪、三世纪一直到四世纪期间逐渐确立下来。

sentences.en: And, of course, once you've worked out that the incarnation is the 25th of March, then nine months on from that is the 25th of December.
sentences.zh: 当然，一旦你确定了道成肉身是在3月25日，那么九个月后就是12月25日。

sentences.en: And I think that that is how you get it.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它的由来。

sentences.en: And that's absolutely what you would expect.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是你所预料到的。

sentences.en: Because you would expect, you know, this is unbelievably holy for Christians.
sentences.zh: 因为你会预料到，你知道，这对基督徒来说是极其神圣的。

sentences.en: They're not going to nick it from the worship of a sun or from Saturn.
sentences.zh: 他们绝不会从太阳崇拜或农神崇拜那里剽窃它。

sentences.en: And I think the whole, you know, as I said,
sentences.zh: 我认为整个，你知道，正如我所说，

sentences.en: the whole reason why they start celebrating Christmas is because it's about one faction of Christians trying to make a point to another faction of Christians.
sentences.zh: 他们开始庆祝圣诞节的全部原因，是因为这是基督徒的一个派系试图向另一个派系表明观点。

sentences.en: Those are the people that they're conscious of.
sentences.zh: 那些才是他们所关注的人。

sentences.en: They're not interested in what pagans are doing.
sentences.zh: 他们对异教徒在做什么不感兴趣。

sentences.en: So they're basically reminding the other Christians they're saying Christ was human as well as divine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是在提醒其他基督徒，他们在说基督既是人也是神。

sentences.en: And let's have a massive party on his birthday to remind.
sentences.zh: 让我们在他的生日举行一场盛大的派对来提醒大家。

sentences.en: Well, not have a party, but I think at that point, because we don't really know how they're celebrating it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是举行派对，但我认为在那个时候，因为我们并不真正知道他们是如何庆祝的。

sentences.en: So we don't know what they were doing when they start celebrating Christmas.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不知道他们开始庆祝圣诞节时在做什么。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 不太清楚。

sentences.en: There's probably a lot of singing hymns and praying.
sentences.zh: 可能有很多唱赞美诗和祈祷。

sentences.en: Probably.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: But I mean, but we know that over the course of the centuries that follow, of course, it becomes the great feast day.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我们知道在随后的几个世纪里，它当然成为了伟大的节日。

sentences.en: It is a time of celebration.
sentences.zh: 这是一个庆祝的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because in the depth of winter, you do want to have a celebration.
sentences.zh: 因为在严冬深处，你确实想要庆祝一番。

sentences.en: But you do.
sentences.zh: 但你确实想。

sentences.en: And I thought, Dominic, that we might end with some Roman festive music.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想我们或许可以用一些罗马节日音乐来结束。

sentences.en: Would you like that?
sentences.zh: 你想要这样吗？

sentences.en: Oh, Tom, I would love that.
sentences.zh: 哦，汤姆，我太想了。

sentences.en: As long as you're not going to be singing, I would really enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 只要你不唱歌，我会非常享受的。

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会唱。

sentences.en: So this is the choir of St. Bartholomew the Great, who last Wednesday, they did a medieval carol service.
sentences.zh: 这是大圣巴塞洛缪教堂的唱诗班，上周三他们举办了一场中世纪颂歌礼拜。

sentences.en: And one of the hymns that they sang was written by St. Ambrose in the 4th century.
sentences.zh: 他们唱的一首赞美诗是圣安布罗斯在四世纪写的。

sentences.en: The 4th century?
sentences.zh: 四世纪？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's a properly Roman hymn.
sentences.zh: 这是一首地道的罗马赞美诗。

sentences.en: And Ambrose is a very Roman figure.
sentences.zh: 安布罗斯是一个非常典型的罗马人物。

sentences.en: He'd been a governor in Milan.
sentences.zh: 他曾是米兰的总督。

sentences.en: And then everyone in Milan said, no, we don't want you as a governor, we want you as a bishop.
sentences.zh: 然后米兰的所有人都说，不，我们不要你当总督，我们要你当主教。

sentences.en: And so he, obedient to that, he became one of the great fathers of the church.
sentences.zh: 于是他顺从了，成为了教会伟大的教父之一。

sentences.en: And he wrote this hymn, Veni Redemptor Gentium, which is come redeemer of the peoples of the world, redeemer of the nations.
sentences.zh: 他写了这首赞美诗《Veni Redemptor Gentium》，意思是“来吧，万民的救赎主，列国的救赎主”。

sentences.en: So it's an Advent hymn, so we probably shouldn't be putting it out on the 25th of December, because of course Christ has come.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一首将临期赞美诗，我们可能不应该在12月25日播放它，因为基督当然已经降临了。

sentences.en: But what the hell?
sentences.zh: 但管他呢？

sentences.en: It's a Roman hymn, it's festive.
sentences.zh: 这是一首罗马赞美诗，很喜庆。

sentences.en: And so I think a perfect way to end this episode and to wish everyone a very, very happy Roman Christmas.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是结束本集并祝愿大家度过一个非常、非常快乐的罗马圣诞节的完美方式。

sentences.en: Well done, Tom.
sentences.zh: 干得好，汤姆。

sentences.en: That was fantastic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Merry Christmas, everybody.
sentences.zh: 祝大家圣诞快乐。

sentences.en: And take it away, please, Ambrose.
sentences.zh: 请开始吧，安布罗斯。

sentences.en: Merry Christmas.
sentences.zh: 圣诞快乐。
